cards.what_happened: Police began looking into a death after an unknown man with head injuries was found. The man was a beggar who had been staying in Minuwangoda. Officers are trying to find out if the injuries came from a road accident or a crime.
details: The source is a newswire report. Police started an investigation after a body was found. The body was an unidentified man who had injuries to his head.
The body was found in the Walpitamulla area of Minuwangoda. Police said it was found on Monday (16) morning. They said the dead man was a beggar who had been living in Minuwangoda.

Police saw injuries on the man's head and said questions came up about his death. Investigators are trying to know if the injuries were from a road accident or a criminal act. The Minuwangoda Police are doing more investigations.

24 yr old STF officer killed in motorcycle accident in Matale

cards.what_happened: A 24-year-old STF police officer was killed after his motorcycle crashed into a car and then hit a signboard on the Kurunegala–Matale Road in Yatawatta on Monday night. The impact left him with serious injuries, and he later died at Yatawatta Hospital. Police say the accident occurred when the bike collided with the rear of a vehicle traveling in the same direction.
details: The deceased was a 24‑year-old Police Constable attached to the STF’s Parayanalankulam Camp and a resident of Yatawatta. He was riding a motorcycle toward Matale on the Kurunegala–Matale Road when his bike hit the rear of a car moving in the same direction.

After the collision the motorcycle veered off the road and struck a signboard outside a roadside shop, causing severe injuries that required hospital treatment. He was taken to Yatawatta Hospital where he later succumbed to his wounds, and the Yatawatta Police are now conducting further investigations.

Cyclonic Storm Akvan: Warning issued to Naval and fishing communities

cards.what_happened: The Department of Meteorology warned naval and fishing communities not to enter several sea areas because of bad weather from Cyclonic Storm Akvan. The storm strengthened and is expected to get stronger.
details: The Newswire reported that the Department of Meteorology in Sri Lanka gave a warning to naval and fishing communities. It said they should not go into some sea areas because of bad weather from Cyclonic Storm Akvan. The advice was to stay away from the listed sea zones.

The Met Department said the groups should not enter deep sea areas between 5°N and 18°N and 80°E and 95°E. It also named sea areas from Kankasanthurai to Pottuvil via Trincomalee and Batticaloa. People already working there were told to go to safer places.

The warning came after a deep depression over the Southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal became Cyclonic Storm Akvan. The storm was about 640 kilometres from Trincomalee at around 11.30 p.m. yesterday (16). It is expected to become a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by 5.30 p.m. today (17), before strengthening further into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by November 19, and it may cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts in India between Nellore and Tuni around 11.30 a.m. on November 20.

The department said showers or thunder may happen at several sea places around Sri Lanka today. It expected north-westerly or westerly winds of 30–40 kmph, with speeds increasing up to 60 kmph at times in affected sea areas, and wind speeds may reach 50 kmph in other sea areas around the island. It also warned that eastern and northeastern coastal stretches could become rough at times, other sea areas may be fairly rough, and strong gusty winds of 60–70 kmph and very rough seas were possible during thunder, while fishing and naval groups were urged to stay vigilant and follow future forecasts and advisories.

The Department of Meteorology asked naval and fishing communities to remain vigilant and follow future weather forecasts and advisories.

Rs. 451 billion, zero loans: Cabinet approves two new expressways

cards.what_happened: The Cabinet approved two new expressway projects worth Rs. 451 billion, to be built without loans using tax revenue. The projects are the Kurunegala–Galewela Expressway, the first section of Phase 4 of the Central Expressway, and the Kahathuduwa–Ingiriya Expressway, the first phase of the proposed Ruwanpura Expressway. Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake announced the approval in a social media post.
details: According to Newswire, Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake said the government is undertaking major expressway development projects worth Rs. 451 billion. He made the announcement in a social media post.
The projects will be financed without any loans, using tax revenue to cover the costs. The minister described the investment as significant for road infrastructure, fully funded through tax revenue.

The Cabinet approved the Kurunegala–Galewela Expressway, which is the first section of Phase 4 of the Central Expressway. It also approved the Kahathuduwa–Ingiriya Expressway, the first phase of the proposed Ruwanpura Expressway.
